overall_interpretation: HEICO is a NEGATIVE-CONTROL for the J-Book Exposure Divergence pattern. Unlike the YSS/IONQ short-thesis archetype (small-cap deriving 80-96% of revenue from a single named Pentagon PE that has been zeroed), HEICO's defense exposure is structurally diversified across hundreds of low-PE-concentration aftermarket positions. The 10-K Item 1 narrative names exactly one specific DoD program of record (F-16) and one specific aircraft platform; everything else is capability-category prose (TWTAs, microwave, RF, EW, rad-hard memory) or aggregate revenue mix (35% defense+space+homeland-sec; ETG 49% defense). For every J-Book-grounded claim that could be tested, pentagon_jbook returned PASS-tier signals (FUNDED_STEADY for F-16 Squadrons PE 0207133F, Electronic Warfare Development PE 0604270F, Ballistic Missile Defense PE 0603881C, Land Based SM-3 PE 0604880C, Space Test Program PE 1206864SF) — i.e., the DoD demand HEICO claims exposure to is actually funded in the forward J-Book. USAspending corroborates $186.8M / 5,462 past DoD awards across HEICO subsidiaries (Robertson Fuel Systems, Santa Barbara Infrared, Sierra Microwave) — so the past-obligated trail is real. Counterparty edgar_fts checks against Lockheed Martin / Northrop Grumman / Raytheon 10-Ks/10-Qs returned ZERO mentions of 'HEICO' (2022-Aug2024), which is expected for a designed-in sub-supplier — HEICO is below the primes' MD&A materiality threshold, which itself is a structural confirmation of the rollup thesis: HEICO is a portfolio of niches, none individually material to any one prime. The Wencor acquisition (claim C9) is confirmed via 27 EDGAR hits on the parent's own filings. Net: no J-Book divergence signal at the 2024-09-01 cutoff; thesis would have to come from the rollup-quality / aftermarket-commercial-aviation side, not from a Pentagon-program-cliff catalyst.
